title: Atomic snapshot migrator and phased channel controller for Private upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Customers running Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) require a zero-downtime, auditable upgrade path that can: apply stateful database/schema changes, move long-running stateful workloads, and perform binary/service upgrades across heterogeneous clusters. Existing upgrade tools either assume immutable infra or rely on fragile hand-run steps that lead to long outages or inconsistent state.

Goal:
Deliver an 'Atomic Snapshot Migrator' + 'Phased Channel Controller' that together provide:
- Coordinated snapshot-and-apply migration for stateful services and metadata (idempotent, resumable, verifiable)
- LTS/release channel awareness (canary -> staged -> LTS) with configurable rollout gates per-customer and per-cohort
- Built-in preflight checks and safety invariants with automatic rollback triggers on critical failures
- Operational telemetry and audit trail for each migration transaction (trace-id, step-level timing, affected nodes)

Scope / what we'll build in this ticket:
1) Snapshot migrator service:
   - Export consistent state snapshots (DB, config, KV caches) using quiesce hooks and log-consistent markers for offset-based replay.
   - Apply path with idempotent steps and validation hooks. Each step has a well-defined undo where possible.
   - Resume semantics: detect partial migration, validate, and continue or safely abort.

2) Phased channel controller:
   - Channel definitions (alpha, canary, staged, LTS) tied to release metadata and compatibility matrix.
   - Gate engine: simple rule language (percent, time-window, error-threshold, custom predicate via webhook) to promote cohorts.
   - Orchestration: coordinate cohorts across zones/regions with backoff and automatic fallback to last-known-good model.

3) Safety and rollback:
   - Multi-tier health probes (process, readiness, application invariants) evaluated during rollout.
   - Automatic rollback policy that can run a reverse migration path or pin to prior images/configs when reversibility is supported.
   - Manual abort with documented remediation playbook.

4) Telemetry & audit:
   - Event stream for migration lifecycle events (started, step-complete, validation-pass/fail, promoted, rolled-back).
   - Per-migration trace id correlated with logs, console UI, and support tickets.
   - Post-mortem metadata export (what changed, when, who triggered, duration).

Acceptance criteria:
- Run a full upgrade in a preprod vpc-onprem cluster: snapshot -> apply -> validate -> promote to staged (50% traffic) -> promote to LTS (100%). All steps must be resumable after controller restart.
- Zero unacknowledged data loss for snapshot-replay path in our test harness (synthetic traffic + integrity hashes).
- Telemetry visible in Console: migration timeline, step durations, and a trace id link to logs.
- Gate triggers allow automatic rollback when error-rate exceeds threshold within 10 minutes of promotion.

Non-goals for this ticket:
- Building a complete UI. We'll provide API endpoints and prototype console links.
- Handling every possible DB engine: we'll implement adapters for Postgres and CockroachDB as the first targets and provide extension hooks for others.

Implementation notes / design decisions considered:
- Prefer snapshot+replay over live, in-place schema migrations for many stateful components because it gives clearer undo and verification semantics for heterogeneous on-prem customers.
- Use a coordinator + worker pattern: coordinator holds migration graph and state in an internal, versioned store (CRD/metadb), workers are short-lived executors on customer cluster. This avoids long-lived locks.
- Store migration manifests as versioned artifacts (release-tag + migration-hash). This helps traceability and supports channel pinning.

Planned tasks (rough order):
- Spec: migration manifest schema, step type catalog, and gate rule DSL (owner: Maya)
- Coordinator prototype: CRD/metadb model + REST API (owner: Diego)
- Snapshot/export adapters for Postgres/Cockroach (owner: Priya Singh)
- Apply/resume worker and undo primitives (owner: Omar Nazari)
- Gate engine implementation and test harness for promotion/rollback (owner: Diego + SRE)
- Telemetry events and Console integration hooks (owner: Analytics team)
- End-to-end test harness and chaos scenarios (owner: QE)

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: irreversible schema migration leaves cluster in bad state. Mitigation: require an explicit 'destructive' flag and block by default for customers without backups; provide a dry-run mode that runs all validation steps without committing.
- Risk: migration coordinator becoming single point of failure. Mitigation: coordinator is designed to be stateless by storing state in customer metadb and using leader election for active controller.
- Risk: long-running migrations during traffic spikes. Mitigation: gate engine integrates with traffic shaping and can pause promotions during high latency windows.

Operational runbook (summary):
- Preflight: run preflight-checks CLI; ensure snapshot backup file created and checksum uploaded.
- Start migration: create migration manifest and POST to coordinator; record trace id.
- Monitor: use Console trace to watch step-level status. If any critical validation fails, controller auto-triggers rollback.
- Post-mortem: export migration report and attach to incident ticket.

Notes on backwards compatibility and LTS channels:
- Releases will publish a migration manifest per release. LTS channel picks manifests marked stable. Pinned customers will only receive manifests that pass compatibility gates and a special 'compatibility shim' will be applied when older agents need binary shims.

QA plan:
- Unit tests for idempotency of each step type.
- Integration tests that simulate network partitions and controller restarts to ensure resume semantics.
- Synthetic data integrity tests for snapshot replay.
- Canary run for 10 internal customers on canary channel before broader staged rollout.

Documentation & customer comms:
- PRD and migration operator guide in Confluence (link to be added).
- Customer-facing KB: how to opt into channels, dry-run, and request rollback.

Open questions (next triage):
- Should destructive migrations require an out-of-band signed approval for on-prem? (security/customer ops tradeoff)
- Level of granularity for cohort definition (node-level vs zone-level vs customer-level).
- How to represent complex undo steps that cannot be fully automated (runbook vs partial rollback).
